newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti capital gain less from Acorn sale.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti capital gain less from Acorn sale.

text.p: Italy's information technology group Olivetti said that the capital gain from the sale of a stake in British-based Acorn Computer Group Plc in June 1996 was less than orginally expected.
In a statement, Olivetti said the capital gain from the equity swap deal with Lehman Brothers Finance SA was 57.5 billion lire instead of the 64 billion lire expected at the time of the sale.

But Olivetti said that the reduction of 6.5 billion lire was fully covered in a fund of 85 billion lire set up in the first half of 1996 to cover the possible reduction in capital gains in the sale of assets.
In June 1996, Olivetti Telemedia sold the 13.25 million share stake in Acorn, bringing its stake down to 31 percent of Acorn, but still leaving it as Acorn's largest shareholder.
On Wednesday, Lehman said it had sold 11.7 million shares in Acorn and said this was the remainder of the 14.7 percent stake it bought from Olivetti Telemedia in June 1996.
Lehman had hedged its position on Acorn last year via a derivative contract with Olivetti before selling the stake onto investors and it said following the sale the derivative contract would end.
